title: In Wine Country, Sales Are Down and Fraud is Rampant
partialText: The industry’s murky supply chain has long attracted scammers and con artists. In the words of one expert, “Wine and fraud go hand in hand.”

title: Thousands of EV Car Leases Are Ending Soon, Giving Buyers a More Affordable Option
partialText: The leases on hundreds of thousands of battery-powered cars and trucks will end in the next three years, and many will end up on used-car lots.

title: If On Shoes Are for Everyone, Are They Still Ons?
partialText: The company finds itself at a critical juncture that others have botched: How does it stay a brand for serious athletes while keeping up its breakneck growth?

title: SiriusXM Said to Be in Early Talks to Acquire iHeartMedia
partialText: A deal, which was described by two people familiar with the discussions, would unite two major providers of traditional and satellite radio.

title: 31 Sloths Acquired by an Orlando Animal Attraction Died, Officials Say
partialText: Many of the deaths were attributed to a lack of heat at an unauthorized warehouse that Sloth World was using, officials said.

title: The ‘Lasting Damage’ of Pirro’s Investigation of the Federal Reserve and Powell
partialText: The Trump administration’s attacks on the Federal Reserve have rattled confidence in the central bank’s ability to operate independently before a leadership transition.

title: Over 200,000 Heated Socks Sold at Costco Recalled After Reports of Burns
partialText: The socks, from the brand 32 Degrees, were linked to reports of first- and second-degree burns, according to U.S. product safety regulators.

title: Inside Trump and David Ellison’s Private Party in Washington
partialText: The gathering included executives and leading journalists from CBS News, which Paramount owns, and the head of the Justice Department, which is reviewing the acquisition.

title: Judge Imposes Sanctions on Plaintiff and Her Lawyer in Suit Against Billionaire Leon Black
partialText: A federal judge said the lawyer representing an unnamed plaintiff who accused the billionaire investor of abusing her had “lied repeatedly to the court.”

title: How Jet Fuel Shortages Could Affect Summer Travel to Europe and Beyond
partialText: Facing sky-high fuel costs linked to the war in Iran, airlines are cutting routes and raising prices. European vacations are looking a lot less affordable.

title: Trump Says He Dislikes Prediction Markets. His Family Invests in Them.
partialText: The White House has warned staff not to wager on government decisions, but his family’s involvement with these firms undermines the president’s message.

title: What Are Prediction Markets, and Why Are They Causing Controversy?
partialText: The indictment of a soldier who bet on the U.S. operation to capture President Nicolás Maduro of Venezuela put renewed focus on a new way to gamble, and a new way to cheat.

title: $450 Million Worth of Newhouse Trophies Come to Christie’s
partialText: A special May evening sale will feature 16 artworks from the museum-quality collection of the Condé Nast chief S.I. Newhouse Jr.

title: As Trump Officials Pushed Health Savings Accounts, RFK Jr. Aide Ran Wellness Company Poised to Benefit
partialText: Calley Means remained president of a company that relied on health savings accounts last year as the Trump administration developed policies to expand them.

title: It Was Just a Podcast. Now, It’s Kelce Land.
partialText: When Amazon gutted its podcast company, it built a new department that made creators kings, starting with the football stars Jason and Travis Kelce.

title: Polymarket Bets on Paris Temperature Prompt Investigation After Unusual Spikes
partialText: The authorities said a Paris airport weather sensor may have been tampered with as large wagers were placed on the betting site.

title: The Peril of Piloting Ships Through the Strait of Hormuz
partialText: Controllers for shipping companies face a daunting decision as they try to free vessels trapped in the Persian Gulf: “Basically you’re sending someone unarmed into war.”

title: Justice Department Drops Criminal Investigation of Fed Chair Jerome Powell
partialText: The decision to end the inquiry into Jerome H. Powell’s handling of the Federal Reserve’s renovation could allow Kevin M. Warsh, the president’s pick for Fed chair, to be confirmed.

title: How Kevin Warsh Could Shrink the Fed’s Footprint in Financial Markets
partialText: President Trump’s nominee to become the next chair of the Federal Reserve wants to overhaul the central bank, including its more than $6 trillion balance sheet.

title: Why Everyone, Including Trump, Is Talking About Airline Mergers
partialText: A few carriers are making a lot of money while many are struggling. President Trump and industry executives seem to think mergers may be the answer.

title: Ignoring the War Has Been Working for Long-Term Investors
partialText: The U.S. stock market’s quick rebound this month may be fragile, but riding out the market’s disconcerting waves has been a sound strategy.

title: A.I. Is Forcing More Belt-Tightening at Big Tech
partialText: The growing expense of keeping up in the artificial intelligence race is driving technology companies, young and old, to cut costs.

title: A.I. Start-Ups From Canada and Germany Merge to Take On Silicon Valley
partialText: Cohere is acquiring Aleph Alpha in a deal aimed at customers uneasy about the dominance of American companies in artificial intelligence.

title: Tariffs Raised Consumers’ Prices, but the Refunds Go Only to Businesses
partialText: Many families felt the sting of the president’s now-illegal tariffs, but companies have said little about whether they will share the $166 billion coming back to them.

title: Who’s Getting a Tariff Refund?
partialText: Following a Supreme Court ruling that struck down several Trump administration tariffs, importers have begun applying for their share of $166 billion in refunds. As our economic policy reporter Tony Romm explains, consumers are unlikely to see much of that money returned to their own pockets.

title: Sam Altman’s Next High-Wire Act: Getting OpenAI to Make More Money
partialText: Mr. Altman, who has faced criticism over OpenAI’s direction, has culled company projects and is trying to be more disciplined with strategy.

title: Where to Enjoy an Airport Shower After a Long Flight
partialText: Affordable arrivals lounges offer amenities like nap pods and showers where weary passengers can freshen up. You may never start a vacation the same way again.

title: How Elon Musk Used SpaceX to Benefit Himself and His Businesses
partialText: The rocket maker has been a useful financial tool for Mr. Musk, providing the billionaire with loans and aiding his struggling companies, a Times examination found.

title: Who’s Who in ‘Michael’: A Guide to the Characters
partialText: A new Michael Jackson biopic, with the star’s nephew Jaafar Jackson in the title role, is packed with famous musical figures. These are some of them.

title: DeepSeek’s Sequel Set to Extend China’s Reach in Open-Source A.I.
partialText: Chinese companies have embraced making their most advanced artificial intelligence models available to all.

title: War and Sanctions Accelerate China’s Currency Push
partialText: China’s bid to build a renminbi-based financial system beyond the U.S. dollar’s reach is gaining traction as a way to sidestep sanctions.

title: Pentagon Fires Stars and Stripes Newspaper’s Ombudsman
partialText: The newspaper’s ombudsman, Jacqueline Smith, said she had been given no reason for her dismissal.

title: Soldier Used Classified Information to Bet on Maduro’s Ouster, U.S. Says
partialText: Federal prosecutors say that Sgt. Gannon Ken Van Dyke, who was involved in the operation to oust Nicolás Maduro from power in Venezuela, used the information to place bets on a prediction market.

title: Nike to Cut 1,400 Jobs as Part of Its Turnaround Plan
partialText: Most of the layoffs will affect tech workers as the athletic giant tries to reverse a yearslong sales slump. It’s the second round of cuts this year.

title: Microsoft Targets About 7% of Its U.S. Workers With Buyout Offer
partialText: The tech giant is offering long-serving employees early retirements as it continues to invest aggressively in artificial intelligence.

title: Two Litigation Partners Depart Paul Weiss
partialText: Kannon Shanmugam and Masha Hansford are the latest in a string of litigators who have left the influential New York law firm.

title: New Gene Therapy Enables Children With a Rare Form of Deafness to Hear
partialText: The treatment, the first of its kind, was approved by the Food and Drug Administration on Thursday. “Our baby was born deaf, and now he can hear,” said one parent.

title: Congress May Finally Recognize That Mobile Homes Aren’t Really That Mobile
partialText: An obscure federal rule requires manufactured homes to be built on a chassis, making them more costly. A bill in Congress would remove the mandate, enacted five decades ago.

title: How We Cover the White House Correspondents’ Dinner
partialText: The annual black-tie event attracts Hollywood stars, reporters and politicians for an irreverent night celebrating press freedom.

title: Warner Bros. Discovery Shareholders Approve Paramount Deal
partialText: The vote brings the tech scion David Ellison one step closer to uniting some of the world’s biggest news and entertainment properties.

title: Investors Fret Over Tesla’s $25 Billion A.I. Bet
partialText: Elon Musk’s electric vehicle company said that it needs to spend big on artificial intelligence and robots. Wall Street is worried about the bill.

title: Why Diesel Has Become a Much Bigger Economic Problem Than Gasoline
partialText: The war in Iran has disrupted supplies of diesel, used to power trucks and heavy equipment, much more than gasoline, which is primarily used in passenger cars.

title: As U.S. Brands Stumble, China Wins Over Young Indonesians
partialText: A new generation of Indonesian consumers view Chinese brands as high-tech and of good quality, a departure from the days when “made in China” was associated with cheap goods.

title: Controversies and Production Issues Around ‘Michael,’ the Jackson Biopic, Explained
partialText: Reshoots, reluctant studios and family holdouts: the production faced many issues. But now the box office is expected to be huge.

title: Some Labubu Dolls Contain Cotton Banned by Forced Labor Law, Testing Shows
partialText: A test verified by The New York Times found that clothes for some of the viral dolls contained cotton from the Xinjiang region of China, which is banned in the United States.

title: Oil Prices Rise and Stocks Slide Amid Uncertainty Over Next Steps in War
partialText: Investors wrestled with uncertainty about the cease-fire between the United States and Iran.

title: Heidi O’Neill, Formerly of Nike, Will Be New Lululemon’s New CEO
partialText: Heidi O’Neill will join the maker of yoga pants and other athletic clothing in September.

title: Tesla Profit Rises but Remains Below Earlier Highs
partialText: The company is investing in robots and self-driving taxis that are not yet generating significant sales.

title: Iran Again Tightens Its Grip on Shipping in the Strait of Hormuz
partialText: Traffic in the strait has all but halted as Iran renews its attacks, striking two vessels on Wednesday. More than 300 ships linked to Iran have passed through the strait since the war began.
